dimensions.title: Interface surface
dimensions.rationale: Not yet: Launchable by other programs with input: command-line arguments, a URL scheme or file associations.
gaps: L1 Launchable by other programs with input: command-line arguments, a URL scheme or file associations. (no arguments, URL scheme or file associations)
dimensions.question: Can another program use it through a documented, machine-readable surface?

requirements.text: Launchable by other programs with input: command-line arguments, a URL scheme or file associations.
requirements.note: no arguments, URL scheme or file associations

requirements.text: An automation interface: AppleScript, App Intents/Shortcuts, D-Bus, COM, IPC commands, or a local API.
Its functions run without the GUI (a headless/batch mode or a companion CLI).
The automation interface is specified machine-readably (an AppleScript sdef, D-Bus introspection XML, App Intents, an OpenAPI spec, MCP).

dimensions.title: Contract stability
dimensions.rationale: Releases are versioned (semver tags or versioned changelog sections).
gaps: L2 A changelog exists and marks breaking changes. (no changelog)
dimensions.question: Can integrators rely on it not changing under them?

requirements.text: Releases are versioned (semver tags or versioned changelog sections).
A changelog exists and marks breaking changes.
A deprecation mechanism is used in code (warnings, @deprecated, Deprecation/Sunset headers) or the API is versioned.
requirements.note: no deprecation mechanism or API versioning

requirements.text: Across tagged releases, no OpenAPI operation, CLI option or __all__ symbol was removed without first being deprecated.

dimensions.title: Events
dimensions.rationale: Not applicable: no service and no long-running CLI mode (batch CLIs, libraries and desktop apps have no events).
dimensions.question: Can others react to state changes without polling?

dimensions.title: Identity
dimensions.rationale: Credentials are kept in the OS credential store (Keychain, Credential Manager, Secret Service), not in plain files.
gaps: L2 Automation and headless runs can authenticate without the GUI (credentials from the environment). (only the GUI can authenticate)
dimensions.question: Can a machine act with its own revocable, least-privilege identity?

requirements.text: Credentials are kept in the OS credential store (Keychain, Credential Manager, Secret Service), not in plain files.
Automation and headless runs can authenticate without the GUI (credentials from the environment).
No output or log statement includes a credential.
Several profiles or scoped credentials per target.

dimensions.title: Data portability
dimensions.rationale: Not applicable: owns no persistent data.
dimensions.question: Can its data get in and out, in bulk, in open formats, with an explicit schema?

dimensions.title: Agent ergonomics
dimensions.rationale: Not yet: In headless mode, failures end with a non-zero exit status instead of a dialog.
gaps: L1 In headless mode, failures end with a non-zero exit status instead of a dialog. (no headless mode for automated callers)
dimensions.question: Can an automated caller use it without guessing, and recover from failure?

requirements.text: In headless mode, failures end with a non-zero exit status instead of a dialog.
requirements.note: no headless mode for automated callers

requirements.text: In headless mode, data goes to stdout and diagnostics to stderr.
requirements.note: no headless mode for automated callers

requirements.text: Documented exit statuses distinguish error classes, and headless output is machine-readable (JSON).
requirements.note: no headless mode for automated callers

requirements.text: Dry-run for side-effecting operations, and agent docs.
requirements.note: no headless mode for automated callers

dimensions.title: Embeddability
dimensions.rationale: Distributed for unattended installation: a package manager (Homebrew cask, winget, Chocolatey, Flathub, Snap) or release artifacts built in CI.
gaps: L4 Settings can be managed without the GUI: documented environment variables or config file, macOS defaults/MDM profiles, or Windows policies. (settings only change through the GUI)
dimensions.question: Can another system run and compose it without a human?

requirements.text: Buildable from source with documented steps (a README with commands).
Packaged as an installer (dmg/pkg, MSI/MSIX, AppImage/Flatpak/Snap, electron-builder, Tauri bundle, PyInstaller).
Distributed for unattended installation: a package manager (Homebrew cask, winget, Chocolatey, Flathub, Snap) or release artifacts built in CI.
Settings can be managed without the GUI: documented environment variables or config file, macOS defaults/MDM profiles, or Windows policies.
requirements.note: settings only change through the GUI

dimensions.title: Extensibility
dimensions.rationale: Not yet: Internal seams: a registry, registration function or plugin manager.
gaps: L1 Internal seams: a registry, registration function or plugin manager. (no registry or registration function)
dimensions.question: Can behaviour be added without modifying the code?

requirements.text: Internal seams: a registry, registration function or plugin manager.
The docs show how to add behaviour through those seams (even in-tree).
Out-of-tree extensions are discovered (entry points, a plugin directory, configuration) without editing the package.
requirements.note: extensions must be added inside the package

requirements.text: The extension API is versioned, has lifecycle hooks, and has example extensions.

dimensions.title: Observability
dimensions.rationale: Not yet: Writes logs through a standard logger (os_log/Logger, electron-log, logging, Qt categories).
gaps: L1 Writes logs through a standard logger (os_log/Logger, electron-log, logging, Qt categories). (no standard logging)
dimensions.question: Can an operator, or an orchestrating agent, tell whether it works and why not?

requirements.text: Writes logs through a standard logger (os_log/Logger, electron-log, logging, Qt categories).
Log verbosity can be raised for diagnosis (--verbose/--debug, a log-level setting).
Crashes are reported (Sentry, Crashpad/Breakpad, Crashlytics, MetricKit).
Tracing or metrics (OpenTelemetry).

dimensions.title: Change legibility
dimensions.rationale: Not yet: A README and some tests.
gaps: L1 A README and some tests. (no tests)
dimensions.question: Can an agent change it safely with limited context?

requirements.text: A README and some tests.
CI runs the tests; applications pin dependencies (libraries and zero-dependency projects are exempt).
At least 90% of modules fit 32k tokens and no file exceeds 12k; test/source token ratio at least 0.3; at least 70% of the code is typed.
requirements.note: test/source token ratio 0.00 < 0.3; 47% of code is typed (< 70%)

requirements.text: No import cycles, and agent docs (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, llms.txt).
